title: Filling in the blanks with matrix factorization
sub: Rows are people, columns are films. Two hidden dimensions, learned by alternating least squares.

frames.caption: Six people, six films, ratings 1-5. Nine ratings are unknown (?). The bet behind matrix factorization: tastes have only a few hidden dimensions, so the table should be a product of two thin matrices, one row of numbers per person and per film.
Alternate: holding the film vectors fixed, each person's vector is an ordinary least-squares fit to the ratings they gave; then hold people fixed and fit each film. Iteration 1.
Iteration 2: the fit to the known ratings tightens.
Iteration 4. The blanks now hold predictions: each is just person-vector · film-vector.
Converged (training error 0.14). The filled-in cells are the recommendations.

How good are the guesses? Against the true (noise-free) tastes, the predictions for the 9 unknown cells are off by 0.37 stars on average, versus 1.27 for guessing the overall average rating. The model discovered on its own that these people split into thriller fans and animation fans.
